title: NASA Project Life Cycle, Key Decision Points, Technical Reviews and TRLs
description: Space flight project life-cycle phases (Pre-Phase A to F), KDPs, the life-cycle technical reviews of Table 6.7-1 (plus TRR), the SE product maturity expected at each review (Table 3.0-1) and the TRL scale (Figure G.4-1), as presented in NASA SE Handbook Rev 2.

extraction.method: pdftotext -layout of the pinned PDF with anchor-based page location; Table 3.0-1 and Figure G.4-1 transcribed from pdftoppm page renders and cross-checked against recovered text tokens (scripts/extract/nasa_se.py)
extraction.notes: Phase purposes, review purposes/timing/results and KDP text are paraphrases. TRL descriptions and product-maturity cells are verbatim from the figures. Entrance and success criteria for each review are NOT reproduced in the handbook; it points to NPR 7123.1 Appendix G tables, recorded here as 'criteria_reference'. TRR is not a row of Table 6.7-1; it is taken from the Section 5.3 note and the Appendix B glossary. Life cycles for IT (NPR 7120.7), R&T (NPR 7120.8) and software (NPR 7150.2) differ and are not modelled.

groups.title: Project life-cycle phases (Pre-Phase A to F)

items.title: Pre-Phase A: Concept Studies
items.text: Produce a broad spectrum of mission ideas and alternatives from which new programs/projects can be selected; determine feasibility, develop mission concepts, draft system-level requirements, assess performance/cost/schedule feasibility and identify technology needs and scope.
items.typical_outcomes: Feasible system concepts (simulations, analyses, study reports, models, mockups)
key_activities: Identify key stakeholders and capture expectations as needs, goals and objectives (NGOs)
Define measures of effectiveness
Develop and baseline the Concept of Operations
Perform trade-offs and analyses of alternatives
Identify risk classification and initial technical risks
Develop preliminary SEMP and baseline the Technology Development Plan
Define preliminary verification and validation approach
Prepare proposals incl. high-level WBS and ROM cost, schedule and risk estimates

items.title: Phase A: Concept and Technology Development
items.text: Determine the feasibility and desirability of the suggested system and establish an initial baseline; develop the final mission concept, system-level requirements, needed technology developments and technical management plans.
items.typical_outcomes: System concept definition (simulations, analyses, engineering models and mockups, trade study definition)
key_activities: Develop and baseline top-level requirements and constraints incl. internal and external interfaces
Allocate system requirements to functions and to the next lower level
Validate requirements
Baseline the SEMP, HSI Plan and control plans (risk, CM, data management, S&MA, software)
Develop preliminary Verification and Validation Plan
Develop and baseline mission architecture; perform and archive trade studies
Provide technical cost estimate and range; define the WBS; develop SOWs
Identify, analyze and update risks

items.title: Phase B: Preliminary Design and Technology Completion
items.text: Define the project in enough detail to establish an initial baseline capable of meeting mission needs; develop end-product and enabling-product requirements and a preliminary design for each system structure end product.
items.typical_outcomes: Mockups, trade study results, specification and interface documents, prototypes
key_activities: Develop the preliminary design incl. internal and external interfaces; select a preliminary design solution
Develop operations plans based on the matured ConOps
Report technology development results
Update cost range estimate and schedule data
Identify and update risks
Develop preliminary orbital debris assessment, decommissioning and disposal plans

items.title: Phase C: Final Design and Fabrication
items.text: Complete the detailed design of the system (including operations systems), fabricate hardware and code software; generate final designs for each system structure end product.
items.typical_outcomes: End-product detailed designs, component fabrication and software development
key_activities: Develop and document hardware and software detailed designs; fully document final design and data package
Baseline interface definitions, implementation, integration, V&V and operations plans
Develop/refine procedures for integration, manufacturing/assembly and V&V
Fabricate (or code) the product
Identify and update risks

items.title: Phase D: System Assembly, Integration and Test, Launch
items.text: Assemble and integrate the system (hardware, software and humans) while developing confidence that it meets the system requirements; launch and prepare for operations; transition to use.
items.typical_outcomes: Operations-ready system end product with supporting related enabling products
key_activities: Integrate/assemble components according to the integration plans
Perform verification and validation per the V&V Plan (qualification, acceptance, end-to-end tests)
Resolve V&V discrepancies and baseline the verification and validation report
Prepare and baseline operator's and maintenance manuals and operations handbook
Train operators and maintainers; confirm readiness for flight
Document lessons learned
reviews: System functional and physical configuration audits

items.title: Phase E: Operations and Sustainment
items.text: Conduct the mission to meet the initially identified need and maintain support for that need; implement the mission operations plan.
key_activities: Conduct the prime mission(s) and provide sustaining support
Collect and analyse engineering and science data
Address problem/failure reports; identify and update risks
Apply for mission extensions if warranted
Prepare for deactivation and decommissioning; capture lessons learned

items.title: Phase F: Closeout
items.text: Implement the systems decommissioning/disposal plan developed in Phase E and analyse returned data and any returned samples.
key_activities: Dispose of the system and supporting processes
Baseline the mission final report
Archive data
Capture lessons learned

items.title: Key Decision Point A
items.text: Decision gate at which the decision authority determines readiness to progress from Pre-Phase A to Phase A; decisions may carry liens, and a project failing a KDP may retry after addressing deficiencies or be terminated.

items.title: Key Decision Point B
items.text: Decision gate at which the decision authority determines readiness to progress from Phase A to Phase B; decisions may carry liens, and a project failing a KDP may retry after addressing deficiencies or be terminated.

items.title: Key Decision Point C
items.text: Decision gate at which the decision authority determines readiness to progress from Phase B to Phase C; decisions may carry liens, and a project failing a KDP may retry after addressing deficiencies or be terminated.

items.title: Key Decision Point D
items.text: Decision gate at which the decision authority determines readiness to progress from Phase C to Phase D; decisions may carry liens, and a project failing a KDP may retry after addressing deficiencies or be terminated.

items.title: Key Decision Point E
items.text: Decision gate at which the decision authority determines readiness to progress from Phase D to Phase E; decisions may carry liens, and a project failing a KDP may retry after addressing deficiencies or be terminated.

items.title: Key Decision Point F
items.text: Decision gate at which the decision authority determines readiness to progress from Phase E to Phase F; decisions may carry liens, and a project failing a KDP may retry after addressing deficiencies or be terminated.

items.title: Mission Concept Review
items.text: Affirm the mission need and evaluate the proposed objectives and the concept for meeting them.
items.timing: Completed before entering the concept development phase (Phase A).
items.results: Supports a determination that the mission meets the customer need and merits further study as a candidate Phase A effort.

product_maturity.product: Stakeholder identification and [label truncated in source]

items.title: System Requirements Review
items.text: Evaluate the functional and performance requirements defined for the system and the preliminary program/project plan, and ensure that the requirements and selected concept will satisfy the mission.
items.timing: Conducted during concept development (Phase A), before the SDR or MDR.
items.results: Freezes program/project requirements and leads to a formal decision to proceed with proposal request preparations for project implementation. (Program-level SRR criteria: NPR 7123.1 Table G-1.)

product_maturity.product: Stakeholder identification and [label truncated in source]

items.title: Mission Definition Review / System Definition Review
items.text: Evaluate whether the proposed architecture is responsive to the functional and performance requirements and that the requirements have been allocated to all functional elements of the mission/system (called MDR for robotic projects, SDR for human flight projects).
items.timing: Conducted during concept development (Phase A), prior to KDP B and the start of preliminary design.
items.results: Supports the decision to further develop the architecture/design and any needed technology; the system and its operation are understood well enough to warrant design and acquisition of end items. (Program-level criteria: NPR 7123.1 Table G-2.)

product_maturity.product: Stakeholder identification and [label truncated in source]
Allocation of requirements to next lower level

items.title: Preliminary Design Review
items.text: Demonstrate that the preliminary design meets all system requirements with acceptable risk and within cost and schedule constraints: correct design options selected, interfaces identified, verification methods described, critical system-wide issues resolved.
items.timing: Near the completion of preliminary design (Phase B), as the last review in the Formulation Phase.
items.results: The design-to baseline is approved and the project is authorized to proceed into Implementation and toward final design.

product_maturity.product: Stakeholder identification and [label truncated in source]

items.title: Critical Design Review
items.text: Demonstrate that design maturity supports proceeding with full-scale fabrication, assembly, integration and test, and that the technical effort is on track to meet mission performance requirements within cost and schedule.
items.timing: During the final design phase (Phase C).
items.results: The build-to baseline, production and verification plans are approved; coding of deliverable software and system qualification testing and integration are authorized; open issues have closure actions.

items.title: Production Readiness Review
items.text: For projects producing multiple or similar systems (more than three, or as determined by the project): determine readiness to efficiently produce the required number of systems, with production plans, enabling products and personnel in place.
items.timing: During the final design phase (Phase C).
items.results: The final production build-to baseline, production and verification plans are approved and drawings are released for production.

items.title: System Integration Review
items.text: Ensure segments, components and subsystems are on schedule to be integrated and that integration facilities, support personnel and integration plans and procedures are on schedule.
items.timing: At the end of final design (Phase C), before system assembly, integration and test (Phase D) begins.
items.results: The final as-built baseline and verification plans are approved; drawings released to support integration; integration procedures, GSE, facilities, logistics and personnel ready.

items.title: Test Readiness Review
items.text: Ensure that the test article (hardware/software), test facility, support personnel and test procedures are ready for testing; held (informally early, more formally later) to assess readiness for verification and validation, with tailored entrance/success criteria.
items.timing: Before verification/validation test events; typically several TRRs, listed among Phase D reviews.
items.results: Confirmed readiness and availability of test ranges, facilities, trained testers, instrumentation, integration labs, support equipment and other enabling products.
items.criteria_reference: Tailored by the project (TRRs are an activity of the Technical Assessment Process); see NPR 7123.1 for any required criteria.

items.title: System Acceptance Review
items.text: Verify the completeness of specific end products relative to their expected maturity, assess compliance with stakeholder expectations and ensure sufficient technical maturity to authorize shipment to the operational facility or launch site.
items.timing: Phase D (generally applies to human space flight; robotic projects may hold a pre-ship review).
items.results: The system is accepted by the buyer and shipment and installation for operational use are authorized.

items.title: Operational Readiness Review
items.text: Examine the actual system characteristics and operating procedures; ensure all flight and ground hardware, software, personnel, procedures and user documentation reflect the deployed state.
items.results: The system is ready to assume normal operations.

items.title: Flight Readiness Review
items.text: Examine tests, demonstrations, analyses and audits that determine readiness for a safe and successful flight or launch and subsequent flight operations; ensure flight and ground systems, personnel and procedures are operationally ready.
items.timing: Phase D, before launch (Phase D activities focus on preparing for the FRR/MRR).
items.results: Technical and procedural maturity exists for launch and flight authorization and, in some cases, initiation of operations.

items.title: Post-Launch Assessment Review
items.text: Post-deployment evaluation of readiness to proceed with full, routine operations, including transfer of responsibility from the development to the operations organization.
items.timing: Typically after early flight operations and initial checkout.
items.results: The system is ready to assume in-space operations.

items.title: Critical Event Readiness Review
items.text: Confirm readiness to execute the mission's critical activities during flight operations (e.g., orbit insertion, rendezvous and docking, re-entry, scientific encounters).
items.timing: Before each critical event (established at the discretion of the program).
items.results: The system is ready to assume (or resume) in-space operations.

items.title: Post-Flight Assessment Review
items.text: Evaluate flight activities after recovery, identify all anomalies and determine actions to mitigate or resolve them for future flights (human space flight).
items.results: Report documenting flight performance and recommendations is complete; all anomalies documented and dispositioned.

items.title: Decommissioning Review
items.text: Confirm the decision to terminate or decommission the system and assess readiness for safe decommissioning and disposal of system assets.
items.timing: Normally near the end of routine mission operations; may be advanced or delayed by events or extensions.
items.results: Decommissioning and disposal of system items and processes are appropriate and effective.

items.title: Disposal Readiness Review
items.text: Confirm readiness for the final disposal of the system assets.
items.timing: Held as major assets are ready for final disposal.
items.results: Disposal of system items and processes is appropriate and effective.

items.title: TRL 1
items.text: Basic principles observed and reported

items.title: TRL 2
items.text: Technology concept and/or application formulated

items.title: TRL 3
items.text: Analytical and experimental critical function and/or characteristic proof-of-concept

items.title: TRL 4
items.text: Component and/or breadboard validation in laboratory environment

items.title: TRL 5
items.text: Component and/or breadboard validation in relevant environment

items.title: TRL 6
items.text: System/subsystem model or prototype demonstration in a relevant environment (ground or space)

items.title: TRL 7
items.text: System prototype demonstration in a target/space environment

items.title: TRL 8
items.text: Actual system completed and "flight qualified" through test and demonstration (ground or flight)

items.title: TRL 9
items.text: Actual system "flight proven" through successful mission operations

items: Alignment with and contribution to Agency strategic goals
Adequacy of the integrated cost and schedule estimates and funding strategy
Adequacy and availability of non-budgetary resources
Adequacy of the risk management approach
Identify, plan and conduct phase-to-phase technical reviews
Establish each review's purpose, objective, and entry and success criteria
Establish the makeup of the review team
Identify and resolve action items resulting from the review

trl_rules.system_trl_is_lowest: The TRL of a system is determined by the lowest TRL present in it; elements never integrated as a unit lower the unit's TRL.
trl_rules.heritage: If the architecture and environment have changed, a heritage system's TRL drops to TRL 5, at least initially; further analysis may justify TRL 6 or 7 but not TRL 9.
trl_rules.typical_integration_threshold: Typically TRL 6 (technology demonstrated in a relevant environment) is required for a technology to be integrated into an SE process (glossary).

tailoring.definition: Tailoring seeks relief from SE NPR requirements (results in deviations/waivers documented e.g. via the Compliance Matrix in the SEMP); customization modifies recommended practices and needs no waiver, but significant customization should be documented in the SEMP.
criteria: Criticality of the mission in meeting the Agency Strategic Plan
ways: Eliminate a requirement that does not apply
Eliminate a requirement that is overly burdensome
Scale the requirement to balance implementation cost and project risk
Customize: adjust how each of the 17 SE processes is implemented
Customize: adjust the formality and timing of reviews
tailoring.combining_reviews: A small project may combine SRR and SDR/MDR without an SE NPR waiver as long as the intent of both is accomplished; dropping a required review needs a waiver or deviation; the governing PM NPR may still require one.
